questions.q: Acetaldehyde is treated with a little concentrated H₂SO₄ while the mixture is kept at about 0 °C or below. The main product is:
questions.explain: Cold conditions favour the eight-membered tetramer, metaldehyde (a solid); at room temperature the six-membered liquid trimer paraldehyde is formed instead. Swapping the two names is the usual trap.

questions.q: Formaldehyde reacts with ammonia to give urotropine. How many molecules of HCHO and NH₃ combine, and how many water molecules are lost, per molecule of product?
questions.explain: 6HCHO + 4NH₃ → (CH₂)₆N₄ + 6H₂O. All six oxygens of formaldehyde leave as water, which is why urotropine contains no oxygen.

questions.q: Which statement about the products obtained from acetone with acid is correct?
options: Mesityl oxide is formed from three acetone units with dry HCl
Phorone is formed from two acetone units with dry HCl
Mesitylene is formed from three acetone units with conc. H₂SO₄ on heating
Acetone gives a stable C–O–C cyclic trimer similar to paraldehyde
questions.explain: Three acetone molecules condense with loss of three water molecules to give mesitylene (1,3,5-trimethylbenzene). Mesityl oxide needs two acetone units and phorone three, and ketones do not form stable acetal polymers.

questions.q: A white solid separates slowly from concentrated formalin. It does not give Tollens' test as such but regenerates HCHO on heating. Which identification and structure are correct?
options: Paraformaldehyde, a linear chain HO(CH₂O)ₙH with n about 8–100
Polyoxymethylene, an end-capped chain with n much greater than 100
Formose, a racemic mixture of sugars
questions.explain: The solid that separates from concentrated formalin is paraformaldehyde, an open-chain polymer HO(CH₂O)ₙH that depolymerises to HCHO on heating. Trioxane is the cyclic trimer (metaformaldehyde), not paraformaldehyde.
